headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: nullclaw’s broad write/network/tooling can collide with ai-engineering-hub’s MCP/RAG-oriented outputs, while default workspace and secret-handling surfaces raise compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw exposes MCP, files, stdin/stdout, and browser/web channels, so it can ingest external content by default; ai-engineering-hub is tagged MCP/RAG and may produce content intended for downstream agent use. The pairwise bridge is plausible, but direct documentation of one parsing the other’s outputs is absent, so uncertainty is escalated to medium.
conditions: IF nullclaw reads ai-engineering-hub output from ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ or stdin/stdout without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF either agent forwards raw web or file content into the other’s prompt, instruction hijacking becomes feasible.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of peer outputs; require manual review.
Prefix all cross-agent content with provenance labels.
Strip executable instructions from shared files before reuse.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing middleware between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs, and it has broad network egress plus filesystem access. ai-engineering-hub is an open-source agent repo with MCP/RAG tags and no stated isolation from shared workspaces. If they share a workspace or account, sensitive material can flow from nullclaw into ai-engineering-hub outputs or external calls.
conditions: IF both agents share ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ or another common directory, leakage risk is active.
IF ai-engineering-hub content is sent to a third-party backend while containing copied secrets, exfiltration occurs.
mitigations: Keep separate OS users and separate workspaces.
Remove secrets from shared files before either agent reads them.
Disable network egress for any agent handling secrets.
Rotate any credentials that may have been exposed in shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret redaction at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shells; ai-engineering-hub is a repo-oriented agent artifact that may also manipulate files or git through its MCP/RAG workflows. With no documented locking or coordination between the pair, concurrent writes to the same workspace or repository can corrupt state or overwrite changes.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, conflicting commits or file overwrites can occur.
IF either agent writes to shared workspace files without locks, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git locks or a single-writer policy.
Review diffs before merge.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutexes for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can act on webhooks, APIs, and shell commands, so if it consumes ai-engineering-hub outputs as authoritative, downstream actions can cascade. ai-engineering-hub’s MCP/RAG orientation suggests generated guidance may be reused, but there is no direct evidence of verification steps between them. The pathway exists, yet it is not shown as default-authoritative, so medium fits.
conditions: IF nullclaw uses ai-engineering-hub output as a task plan without validation, errors can propagate.
IF either agent triggers webhooks or shell actions from unverified text, cascading mistakes can occur.
mitigations: Require human approval before actions.
Cross-check outputs against source documents.
Limit automation to read-only mode for shared tasks.
Log and review any action derived from peer output.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool execution.

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles secrets, audit logs, workspace files, and broad networked channels, while ai-engineering-hub is an open-source repo with no stated residency or retention controls. If regulated data enters nullclaw’s workspace, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches; uncertainty is escalated because no controls are documented for the pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into nullclaw’s workspace or logs, retention obligations may be violated.
IF ai-engineering-hub content is stored or forwarded without a DPA/residency control, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces.
Set short log retention and purge logs manually.
Restrict cross-border data flows.
Document data-class handling for both agents.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls.
